items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Driven by Q3 2026 total revenue and reserve income of $865 million—up 17% year-over-year—Circle highlighted the upcoming January implementation of the Genius Act, the mainstream scaling of the Arc blockchain network, and over 150% sequential growth in annualized payment volume on the Circle Payments Network (CPN).

## Q3 Financial Results & Metrics
* **Top-Line Performance:** Total revenue and reserve income reached **$865 million**, up 17% year-over-year and 23% sequentially. This included **$182 million** from the Arc token pre-sale.
* **Profitability & Margins:** Adjusted EBITDA came in at **$317 million**, up 85% year-over-year. Revenue less distribution cost (RLDC) margin was **52.4%** (39.7% excluding the Arc token pre-sale). Net reserve margin stood at **37.8%**, down ~80 bps from Q2 following the hyperliquid arrangement.
* **Operating Expenses:** Adjusted operating expenses were **$139 million**, up 13% year-over-year (driven by Arc, AI investments, and Chelsea FC marketing) but down 5% sequentially.
* **USDC Circulation & Usage:** Average USDC circulation was **$73.3 billion** (up 8% year-over-year; exiting the quarter at **$73.9 billion**). Onchain transaction volume grew **49%** year-over-year to **$13.9 trillion**. USDC carried **79%** of all stablecoin transaction volume globally on roughly 27% of supply.
* **Liquidity & Primary Market:** A record **$28 billion** of USDC was minted and redeemed in Q3 (up 42% year-over-year), averaging ~$2.3 billion per day.
* **Other Digital Assets:** EURC grew **92%** year-over-year to **$413 million**, and USYC grew **230%** to **$2.4 billion** in assets.

## Platform Ecosystem: CPN & Acquisitions
* **CPN Scaling:** Annualized payment volume on CPN reached **$41 billion** at the end of Q3 (up 15x year-over-year). By October 30, it surpassed **$58 billion** (>150% sequential growth). Enrolled financial institutions grew 4x year-over-year to **205**.
* **Enterprise & Tech Integrations:** CPN treasury tools integrated with Kyrie and Tina for SAP ERP customers, launched on Arc mainet as the preferred settlement layer, and expanded managed payments to support AI agents.
* **Tazipe Acquisition:** Circle announced an agreement to acquire Tazipay for **$400 million** in Class A common stock (expected to close in 2027). Tazipay processes **>$25 billion** in annualized payment volume (~60% stablecoin-involved) across 100+ payout markets and 60+ bank/fintech partners.

## Arc Network Launch & Ecosystem
* **Mainnet Go-Live:** Arc mainet launched on September 16 with **11 founding validators** (including BNY, HSBC, Société Générale, State Street, JCB, Mastercard, Moneygram, and Visa) and **>100 applications**.
* **Network Activity:** As of late October, Arc held **~$1.5 billion** in USDC, surBTC, and EURC. Over **$30 billion** of USDC has moved on Arc since launch (~$1 billion/day recently), processing **~500,000 transactions per day** with sub-second finality and fees under one cent paid in USDC.
* **Token Value Accrual (Jeremy Fox-Geen):** Circle captures Arc value through staking rewards, selective token sales, and ecosystem incentives. Additionally, Circle's 25% allocation of Arc token holdings is unreflected on GAAP statements until sold or distributed.

## Strategic Partnerships & Global Expansion
* **Binance Agreement:** Signed a new 5-year partnership alongside a **$100 million equity investment** from Binance in Circle, placing USDC at the center of a platform with 300+ million registered users.
* **Chelsea FC Partnership:** Circle became a principal partner of Chelsea FC, featuring USDC on the front of shirts for the 2026-27 season to reach 650 million fans and 1.2 billion homes globally.
* **Agentic Economy:** Over 99% of agent payments on the X42 protocol settle in USDC, and nearly 2,800 endpoints are listed in Circle's agent marketplace.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Genius Act Implementation:** "In January, the Genius Act goes into effect. That is the moment when digital dollars like USDC become a federally recognized part of the US dollar financial system." — Jeremy Allaire
* **Agentic Capability Timeline:** "By the first quarter of 2027, an agent built on ARC can be found, hired, paid, and trusted for the work it does." — Jeremy Allaire
* **Full-Year 2026 Other Revenue Guidance:** Reaffirming full-year guidance of **$310 to $330 million**, which includes **$182 million** from the Arc token pre-sale and **$130 to $150 million** from the remainder of products (Jeremy Fox-Geen).
* **Full-Year RLDC Margin Guidance:** Reaffirming full-year range of **41.7% to 43.7%**, with full-year RLDC margin excluding Arc expected near the midpoint of the original **38% to 40%** range (Jeremy Fox-Geen).
* **Operating Expenses Trend:** Adjusted operating expenses are trending towards the high end of the original **$570 to $585 million** range (Jeremy Fox-Geen).
* **Tazipay Transaction Closure:** The Tazipay acquisition is expected to close in **2027** (Jeremy Allaire).

## Notable Quotes
> "We measure ourselves not only by what we sell but also by what others build and grow on our platform. This is not just about payments and it's not just about digital dollars. It is about multiple compounding flywheels on one platform."
> — Jeremy Allaire

> "The traffic of CPN and the settlement volumes of CPN, we will be moving more and more onto ARC... We want these bit numbers to be very very big with huge network effects and huge velocity with very very low unit costs."
> — Jeremy Allaire

items.title: Confronting Our AI Future: Closing Keynote "Discovery Loop" with Jeff Dean and Fei-Fei Li
items.summary: Jeff Dean and Fei-Fei Li discuss the transition from base AI models to automated discovery loops capable of self-improvement in science and engineering, exploring the balance between technical hype and reality, the limits of recursive self-improvement, and the imperative to design AI for broad societal benefit.
items.content_text:
### TL;DR
Jeff Dean and Fei-Fei Li discuss the transition from base AI models to automated discovery loops capable of self-improvement in science and engineering, exploring the balance between technical hype and reality, the limits of recursive self-improvement, and the imperative to design AI for broad societal benefit.

## Company Mission and Origins: Discovery Loop
* **Mission and Approach:** Founded as a Public Benefit Corporation, Discovery Loop aims to build automated AI systems that solve complex problems in machine learning, science, and engineering by automating traditional experimental loops.
* **Leadership and Team:** Co-founded by Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat, Quoc Le, and Oriol Vinyals—former Google leaders and core contributors to foundational infrastructure, TPUs, and AI models like Gemini and AlphaFold.
* **Founding Metrics:** Within its first three weeks, the team conducted 400 interviews on University Avenue, established an office in the former Zibibo restaurant, built a custom agent-first infrastructure, and launched roughly 20 automated improvement loops.
* **Productivity Goals:** The company's immediate goal is to make domain experts 20x to 50x more productive through agent-human collaboration.

## Technical Foundations: Self-Improvement vs. Recursive Self-Improvement
* **Self-Improving Systems:** Systems given a specific goal and a measurable objective (like improving ML model accuracy) to iteratively test and refine approaches without altering the base system proposing the next steps.
* **Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI):** The process where a self-improving system enhances the base system itself, creating a faster cycle of capability growth.
* **Physical and Computational Limits:** Both speakers cautioned against the hype of infinite acceleration; RSI is bounded by real-world physics, compute constraints, and the time required to run computations and evaluate data.
* **Target Domains:** Initially focusing on digital domains where the entire experimental loop can be accelerated—specifically machine learning research, machine learning engineering, and hardware design.

## Scientific Discovery, Math, and Changing Paradigms
* **Digital vs. Physical Science:** While physical processes are harder to speed up, digital-first domains allow automated loops to run tens of thousands of experiments and scale quality and volume simultaneously.
* **Automated Mathematics:** Recent breakthroughs by OpenAI and others demonstrate that agent-based systems can solve unsolved math problems, though current proofs often lack the elegance sought by human mathematicians.
* **Historical Milestones:** June 12, 2017 marked the release of the Transformer paper on arXiv, a foundational shift for modern generative models.
* **Past Miscalculations:** Jeff Dean noted underestimating how central coding capability would become as a key unlocker for cross-domain AI problem-solving.

## Societal Impact and Human-Centered AI
* **Broad Societal Reach:** Unlike previous technological revolutions confined to 5 or 10 fields, AI simultaneously impacts nearly every sector of society.
* **Key Concerns:** Navigating the dual nature of AI requires addressing employment shifts, economic adaptation, misinformation, and ensuring technology serves all of humanity.
* **Collaborative Framework:** Dean co-authored the paper *Shaping AI's Impact on Billions of People* (shapingai.com) to engage domain experts across seven societal areas, emphasizing that managing AI risks is a shared responsibility among technologists, policymakers, and citizens.

## Notable Quotes
> "If you can drive down iteration time, the time to run one time through these loops, and you can propose and automatically run many experiments, you can learn from each evaluation... you're going to get breakthrough results."
> — Jeff Dean

> "Some people have this illusion that you're going to be able to run this loop infinitely fast, and I just find that kind of implausible... there's just actual physics involved."
> — Jeff Dean

> "I think the one I worry about the most is just how do we capture as much of the upsides of what AI can do across all these different domains while minimizing the downsides... that is not purely a technical problem, that is a technical problem, a regulatory and policy maker problem, a citizen problem."
> — Jeff Dean

items.title: Former NEC Director Gary Cohn: The average citizen today is unhappy with their financial position
items.summary: Gary Cohn discusses the midterm election results, economic affordability pressures, potential bipartisan compromises, and the evolving outlook for AI data centers under a shifting political landscape.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Gary Cohn discusses the midterm election results, economic affordability pressures, potential bipartisan compromises, and the evolving outlook for AI data centers under a shifting political landscape.

## Economic Sentiment & The Affordability Crisis
* **Voter Dissatisfaction:** **Average citizen unhappiness** drives recent election cycles, with consumers voting for change regardless of party affiliation.
  * Sentiment indicators like the Michigan Consumer Sentiment Survey remain at rock bottom due to persistent financial pressure.
  * High-cost necessities—**food, housing, healthcare, and energy**—are squeezing household budgets.
* **The "L-Shaped" Economy:** **Asset owners vs. non-asset owners** divergence has worsened, transitioning from a K-shaped economy to an L-shaped dynamic where the bottom tier remains stagnant despite macroeconomic growth.
* **Macro Growth Disconnect:** Broad economic metrics do not reflect the lived reality of most Americans.
  * **GDP growth:** Reached **3.4%** previously.
  * **Job openings:** JOLTS data showed an increase of **330,000 new job openings**.
  * Despite corporate capex and economic expansion, growth is not working its way down broadly enough to satisfy the public.

## Political Reality & Bipartisan Opportunities
* **Divided Government Constraints:** The current legislative reality features a Democratic House, a Republican-led Senate requiring **60 votes to clear the filibuster** (with John Thune playing a major role), and a Republican president without a veto-proof majority.
* **Potential Compromise Areas:** President Trump may negotiate bipartisan legislation with Democrats in key areas:
  * **Entitlement & Social Security Reform:** Raising the cap on income taxed for Social Security would impose a **12.4% tax increase split evenly (6.2% each) between individuals and companies**, helping shore up the Social Security trust fund before it runs out of money in the early 2030s.
  * **Tariff Policy Codification:** Broad agreement exists on tariffs protecting U.S. workers, manufacturing, and jobs (especially against China), opening the door to pass tariffs through the legislative system rather than relying solely on executive orders.
  * **Border Friction:** Shutting down borders between Canada, Mexico, and the U.S. has proven problematic for policy, representing another area where pragmatic adjustments might be sought.

## AI Data Centers, Infrastructure & Tech Valuations
* **Regional Shifts & Energy Generation:** Texas politics are changing (including a newly elected Democratic governor and senator), impacting companies that recently redomiciled there from Delaware.
  * **Alternative data center hubs:** States like West Virginia offer enormous amounts of natural gas for behind-the-meter electrical generation, allowing data centers to be built without impacting the local grid.
  * **Local tax evaluations:** Jurisdictions must weigh whether data centers bring beneficial tax revenue for teachers and police against potential local roadblocks.
* **Tech Sector Impact & Cash Flow Dynamics:**
  * **Incumbent Advantage:** For mega-cap tech companies like **Amazon, Google, and Meta**, restrictions on new data center builds make existing infrastructure more scarce and valuable, allowing them to charge higher rental rates.
  * **Free Cash Flow Rebound:** Slower data center expansion forces these tech giants away from negative free cash flow (which dropped from **$40–$50 billion** annually into negative territory) and back toward cash-flow-positive operations.
  * **Supplier Uncertainty:** Pure-play hardware and component suppliers (such as CoreWeave or Nvidia) face greater questions regarding where and when the next new data centers will be built.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Social Security Insolvency Timeline:** The Social Security trust fund will run out of money in the **early 2030s**, forcing newly elected senators to address the issue within their current **six-year terms**. — Gary Cohn
* **Electoral Volatility:** If the financial position of the American consumer remains unchanged two years from now, voters will throw incumbents out of office once again. — Gary Cohn

## Notable Quotes
> "The consuming public, hardworking America, the average citizen today, is unhappy with their financial position. And we saw it. We talked about the K shaped economy. ... I almost think the K shaped, the economy has moved to an L. You know, the top goes up and the bottom just sits there at the bottom." — Gary Cohn
> 
> "If you're an Amazon, a Google, a Meta, and you own data centers and you've got them built, and there's now going to be more scarcity than there was before, the data centers you have going in the ground are actually more valuable today than they were yesterday." — Gary Cohn

items.title: Marissa Mayer on Dazzle, AI for Parents, & Letting Agents Into Your Camera Roll | Future Proof
items.summary: Former tech executive Marissa Mayer discusses her new AI consumer startup, Dazzle, which uses smartphone camera rolls as a context layer for personal assistance, while addressing broader industry trends, consumer AI adoption, and the role of AI in legacy and startup operations.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR:** Former tech executive Marissa Mayer discusses her new AI consumer startup, Dazzle, which uses smartphone camera rolls as a context layer for personal assistance, while addressing broader industry trends, consumer AI adoption, and the role of AI in legacy and startup operations.

## The Dazzle App and Photo-Based AI Context
- **Core Premise:** **Dazzle** is an AI personal assistant that learns user tastes, important people, places, and interests entirely from their camera roll.
  - **The "Get It Done" Button:** Users can snap photos of everyday objects or flyers to initiate tasks (buying, fixing, booking, adding to calendars or wallets).
  - **Onboarding Speed:** The average user goes from opening the app for the first time to executing their first agent task in about 45 seconds (**Marissa Mayer**).
- **Surprising Capabilities:** The app detects granular details from background images and user artifacts.
  - **Book Cataloging:** Inferred a user's unowned books and existing author library from bookshelves visible in living room photos (**Marissa Mayer**).
  - **Music and Entertainment Taste:** Identified free symphony concerts in the park from historical photos and concert tees (**Marissa Mayer**).
- **Camera Roll vs. Email:** **Dave Morin** (investor) noted that email represents "somebody else's to-do list for you," whereas the camera roll consists of curated moments and attention chosen deliberately by the user over the lifetime of having a phone (**Marissa Mayer**).
- **Feature Architecture:** Dazzle operates through three main pillars:
  - **Get It Done:** Analyzes recent photos to determine if assistance is needed (active roughly 40% of the time; ignored 60% of the time) (**Marissa Mayer**).
  - **Ideas:** Looks across the historical camera roll to build a context layer and proactively suggest activities, hobbies (e.g., escape rooms like Palace Games in San Francisco), and podcasts (**Marissa Mayer**).
  - **Chat:** Combines the active to-do list and historical context to converse naturally about ongoing projects or purchases (**Marissa Mayer**).
- **Human-in-the-Loop Operations:** Complex, expensive, or high-stakes purchases (like buying a glass tabletop while replacing a window) utilize human customer experience specialists to double-check and prevent errors, while low-dollar or straightforward purchases (like a Starbucks latte) are handled fully by AI agents (**Marissa Mayer**).
- **Privacy and Data Safeguards:** 
  - Uses native iOS controls for full, selective, or no access (**Marissa Mayer**).
  - Automatically deletes and discards sensitive photos (PII, credit cards, intimate images) from servers during secondary processing using a "when in doubt, leave it out" protocol (**Marissa Mayer**).
  - Discard rate is approximately 500 out of 55,000 photos on **Marissa Mayer**'s personal device.

## The Consumer AI Market
- **Market Opportunity:** Citing statistics that only ~6% of AI investment went to consumer applications last year, **Marissa Mayer** notes that the consumer AI market is expected to be twice the size of enterprise by 2030, presenting a massive under-invested opportunity.
- **Demographics and Adoption:**
  - Initial traction spans early adopters, parents managing school schedules, and Gen Z users responding positively to proactive recommendations ("ideas" feature) and ease of use (**Marissa Mayer**).
  - Serves users outside tech-savvy hubs, drawing on Midwestern usability standards (**Marissa Mayer**).
- **Interoperability:** Dazzle features an MCP (Model Context Protocol) to let users hook the app up to Claude or other agent portfolios so context isn't locked in a walled garden (**Marissa Mayer**).

## Enterprise Strategy and Traditional Companies
- **Corporate Tech Adoption:** Board member roles at AT&T, Starbucks, Hilton, and Walmart reveal deep investments in AI leadership and tech transformation (**Marissa Mayer**).
  - **Walmart:** Hired Dan Dancier as Chief AI Officer; operations increasingly mirror classic tech companies (**Marissa Mayer**).
  - **Starbucks:** Hired Anand to lead AI initiatives (**Marissa Mayer**).
  - **Hilton:** Recently appointed a new CTO (**Marissa Mayer**).
- **Application Focus:** Aligns with **Brit Morin**'s thesis that AI is coming for everything people didn't want to do anyway—such as analyzing fiber map anomalies at AT&T or automating customer hold times (**Marissa Mayer**).
- **Leadership Requirements:** Echoing **Kai-Fu Lee**, **Marissa Mayer** agrees that CEOs must take a primary leadership role in driving AI adoption across companies while building specialized teams.

## Internal Operations at Dazzle
- **AI-Native Engineering:** Dazzle has written virtually zero human code in 2026, utilizing multiple coding agents simultaneously to operate at the scale of a much larger team (**Marissa Mayer**).
- **Workflows:** While design starts traditionally via human designers, AI handles multi-screen translation, text-to-reengage optimization for growth conversion rates, and simultaneous data retrieval during meetings (**Marissa Mayer**).
- **Key Metrics:** Focuses primarily on retention over time and frequency of engagement, aiming for a high Daily Active User (DAU) ratio relative to monthly active users (**Marissa Mayer**).

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- The world of consumer AI is expected to be about twice the size of enterprise by 2030 (**Marissa Mayer**).
- Dazzle plans to integrate email context for power users and introduce voice capabilities as token efficiency and model capabilities improve (**Marissa Mayer**).

## Notable Quotes
> "Email is somebody else’s to-do list for you... What’s interesting about your camera roll is you decide what you put there, and you have for as long as you had a phone."
> — **Marissa Mayer**

> "AI isn't coming for your job, but it's coming for everything you didn't want to do anyway."
> — **Brit Morin** (cited by **Marissa Mayer**)

> "I don't think we've written any code this year. Like we have no human written code... probably in 2026."
> — **Marissa Mayer**

items.title: NextEra Energy CEO: Powering AI and Nuclear's Comeback | Podcast | In Good Company
items.summary: Driven by an AI-induced electricity demand projected to increase sixfold over the next 20 years, NextEra Energy CEO John Ketchum is scaling the world's most valuable power company through a massive $60 billion annual capital investment plan and a record-breaking merger with Dominion Energy.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Driven by an AI-induced electricity demand projected to increase sixfold over the next 20 years, NextEra Energy CEO John Ketchum is scaling the world's most valuable power company through a massive $60 billion annual capital investment plan and a record-breaking merger with Dominion Energy.

## AI Boom, Grid Scale, and the Dominion Merger
* **Exploding Power Demand:** 
  * Power demand remained static for decades until the adoption of AI accelerated it exponentially over the past 24 months.
  * Broader demand drivers include the redomestication of manufacturing, semiconductor chip facilities, LNG terminals, and increased residential and transportation consumption.
* **The Dominion Energy Merger:** 
  * NextEra agreed to acquire Dominion Energy to expand its footprint into three key states: Virginia, North Carolina, and South Carolina.
  * Commitments for Virginia include bringing 1,000 new jobs (600 at NextEra, 400 from supplier letters of intent) and building a dual headquarters office tower.
* **Capital Intensity & Supply Chain Advantage:** 
  * NextEra plans to spend **$60 billion a year** ($1 billion a week) on power plants between 2027 and 2032 across a 50-state capital investment plan.
  * Supply chain bottlenecks for turbines, transformers, solar panels, inverters, and batteries are mitigated through massive bulk purchasing; NextEra is already buying equipment through 2030.

## Data Centers: Power Generation vs. Ownership
* **Strategic Focus on Power, Not Real Estate:** 
  * After testing the data center business model by buying a couple of smaller facilities three years ago, NextEra decided to leave data center operations to hyperscalers.
  * Hyperscalers want to own and control their own data centers for cybersecurity and the flexibility to upgrade chips over time.
* **Direct Contracting & Ratepayer Protection:** 
  * Hyperscalers contract directly with NextEra to bring their own dedicated generation rather than drawing down the public grid and driving up retail power prices.
  * NextEra and Dominion have signed ratepayer protection pledges, and Florida codified a protective large-load tariff into statute.
* **Community Relations:** Developers must use closed-loop cooling (reusing water from treatment facilities), pay property taxes, observe noise and setback requirements, and invest locally (e.g., Meta funding $50,000 teacher scholarships in Louisiana).

## Energy Mix: The Return of Gas and Nuclear
* **Fossil Fuels for Baseload:** 
  * While solar is two to three times cheaper than gas, data centers require round-the-clock baseload generation that 4-hour to 8-hour battery storage cannot yet fully supply on its own. NextEra relies on its extensive experience operating the largest US gas-fired generation fleet.
* **Nuclear Restarts:** 
  * NextEra is restarting the Dwayne Arnold nuclear plant, treating the restoration as a "super outage" to supply 25 years of power under an agreement with Google.
* **Small Modular Reactors (SMRs):** 
  * Out of 96 SMR original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), NextEra has narrowed its focus to 3 or 4 technically viable Gen 3 options.
  * SMR deployment requires shared risk among the federal government, the hyperscaler customer, the EPC contractor, and the OEM, as NextEra will not risk shareholder capital on unproven technology.

## Leadership, Culture, and International Strategy
* **Psychologically Safe Dissent:** Ketchum enforces a culture where anyone—from a 25-year-old newbie to a 20-year veteran—is expected to push back on his ideas if they spot a blind spot.
* **Internal Mobility & Career Growth:** Ketchum held 12 different jobs over 24 years, rising from line tax lawyer to CEO. NextEra continuously moves employees across roles to build well-rounded strategic thinkers.
* **Bottom-Up Innovation ("Rewire"):** Annual company programs like *Rewire* (formerly *Accelerate*, *Momentum*, and *Velocity*) rely on employees pitching hundreds of capital and O&M savings ideas directly to an executive steering committee.
* **International Caution:** A past venture into Spanish solar in 2012 resulted in retroactive feed-in tariff cuts during the European recession. Ketchum served as the workout lead for those projects, cementing NextEra's disciplined "toe in the water" approach of making small initial bets before committing significant capital abroad.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **John Ketchum** predicts US electricity demand will increase **sixfold over the next 20 years** (reaching this projection by the mid-2040s).
* **John Ketchum** states NextEra will invest **$60 billion a year** on power plants between **2027 and 2032**.
* **John Ketchum** forecasts that Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) will not reach the "nth-of-a-kind" deployment phase until the **middle of the next decade to later**.

## Notable Quotes
> *"Push back and tell me what you think I'm missing. I don't care if you're a 25-year-old, you know, newbie out of an MBA program or you're somebody who's been with the company for 20 years."* — **John Ketchum**

> *"When you see a headwind in terms of turbine availability, transformers, solar panels, inverters, batteries... when you're buying in bulk and you're usually your supplier's number one customer in the world, you're going to get top flight service."* — **John Ketchum**

> *"If you're going to build a data center, you have to make sure you pay for the power that goes along with it to power that data center. Full stop."* — **John Ketchum**

> *"My advice to young people is do everything that you can to expand your toolkit... Don't worry too much about the first job that you take. Just make sure you're careful to go to a place that will allow you to expand as your interest expands and take on new jobs."* — **John Ketchum**

items.title: The New AI Agents That Shop, Plan, and Gossip
items.summary: As AI assistants evolve from general tools into specialized, multiplayer agent networks, consumers are moving past basic productivity tasks toward complex preferences, social experiences, and trust-building.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR:** As AI assistants evolve from general tools into specialized, multiplayer agent networks, consumers are moving past basic productivity tasks toward complex preferences, social experiences, and trust-building. However, a major hurdle remains: 22% of power user messages center on the fear of trust, privacy, and embarrassing data leaks.

## 1. The State of the Agent Landscape & Meetups
* **The Agent Community Boom:** David Pawlan hosted an agent meetup in San Francisco with over 100 attendees, highlighting that founders and users are craving in-person community and sharing best practices openly rather than acting cagey.
* **Categories of Assistants:** David has tested over 147 different assistants, categorizing them into four primary types:
    * **General**
    * **Work-oriented**
    * **Multiplayer**
    * **Travel**
    * **Finance:** Josh Elman and David noted that finance remains an unfulfilled category waiting to fully take off.

## 2. Trust, Privacy, and "Fences"
* **The Dominant Fear:** Out of 3,600 messages across AI power-user group chats, **22%** of discussions focus on trust as the primary fear in the assistant space.
* **The "Picnic" Analogy & Shane Mack's Leak:** Shane Mack experienced a major privacy failure when his personal agent accidentally crossed into his work environment and blasted his personal finances onto his company Slack. 
    * **The Fence Solution:** Josh Elman emphasized the need for proper "fences" (permissions, boundaries, and monitoring) so personal agents don't bleed into professional channels.
* **Stated vs. Revealed Preferences:** Anish Acharya pointed out that consumers will gladly share all their data for trivial upside (e.g., Hark offering $30 of free pizza in exchange for total access to Google Workspace emails).
* **The Embarrassment Factor:** Josh Elman argued that the true high-stakes fear is social embarrassment (e.g., agents revealing dietary restrictions or miscommunicating on dates), making discretion a mandatory trait for agents.

## 3. Testing Judgment, Cost, and Constraints
* **Flower Delivery Benchmark:** David tested agents on ordering the cheapest flowers for same-day delivery:
    * **Instinct:** Performed exceptionally well at balancing price and time constraints.
    * **Kicker:** Secured an edge by utilizing a local Chrome browser extension.
    * **Season:** Also performed well. 
    * *Other agents failed by prioritizing delivery speed while completely ignoring the price component.*
* **LA Weekend Travel Test:** David tested Grockbot, Dots, and Instinct to book a luxurious yet cost-efficient weekend in LA:
    * **Dots:** Prioritized cost (e.g., choosing a redeye flight).
    * **Grockbot:** Prioritized time and luxury, and was the only agent in a multi-agent chat room that methodically absorbed and implemented value from the other agents' proposals.
* **Onboarding & Memory Portability:** 
    * Only **3%** of 354 surveyed power users use ChatGPT as their primary agent, though it retains massive context.
    * David tested the top 15 benchmarked agents on memory portability: **all but one** allowed users to export their memory file (markdown) to switch assistants easily.

## 4. Commerce, Shopping, and the Rationality Debate
* **Shopping Behavior:** In David's survey, Amazon and retail shopping represented **35%** of what consumers are purchasing through AI.
* **Direct-to-Consumer & Longtail Winners:** Josh Elman and Anish Acharya discussed how agents have infinite patience to search the longtail of the internet, bypassing aggregators and empowering platforms like Shopify to drive direct purchases.
* **Patrick Collison's Rationality Vision vs. Alien Preferences:** 
    * Patrick Collison envisions consumers becoming more rational via agents.
    * Anish Acharya countered that agents will develop their own "alien" revealed preferences—such as an irrational affinity for clean APIs with great documentation.
    * Josh Elman added that "paternalism will kill any product," warning that agents shouldn't force artificial rationality or strict diets on humans who ultimately want to enjoy life.

## 5. Agent-to-Agent Social Networks and Serendipity
* **Agent Gossiping:** Josh Elman highlighted playful agents that chat in the background and share minor updates (like a friend's power being out), creating a healthy "social indirection" and acting as a social lubricant.
* **Multiplayer Apps:** 
    * **Wabby:** Launched recently, allowing users to interact with multiple threads of life and media watchlists.
    * **Tommo:** Features "interest groups" (e.g., grouping users studying for the LSAT) to connect humans based entirely on shared goals.
* **Creating Serendipity:** The panel discussed how agent networks could ultimately form a new kind of social network—moving beyond Facebook's model of connecting only with people you already know, and instead pairing strangers based on real-world desires and complementary goals.

## 6. Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Enterprise Shift (David Pawlan):** The industry will shift more attention toward enterprise use cases over the next few weeks, moving beyond purely consumer-focused assistant hype.
* **Secret Superpowers (Anish Acharya):** Agents will eventually evolve from doing tedious productivity tasks to becoming "dark agents" or "secret superpowers" that help users achieve their deepest personal aspirations and desired identities.

items.title: Waymo’s Bet on a Driverless Future | The Circuit with Emily Chang
items.summary: Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana details how the company is scaling its autonomous ride-hailing fleet and generalizable driver technology despite growing public scrutiny, regulatory hurdles, and safety debates.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR:** Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana details how the company is scaling its autonomous ride-hailing fleet and generalizable driver technology despite growing public scrutiny, regulatory hurdles, and safety debates.

## Leadership & Origins
- **Co-CEO Structure:** Waymo is jointly led by Tekedra Mawakana, who oversees commercialization and market strategy, and Dmitri Dolgov, who leads hardware and software engineering teams.
- **Background & Influence:** Mawakana grew up in Mississippi with family ties to farming, which instilled an understanding of self-sustaining, productive systems. Her career spans law in the mid-1990s and Internet 1.0 leadership roles at AOL, Yahoo, and eBay before joining Waymo.
- **Foundational Lineage:** The company's origins trace back to Google’s original self-driving project and a Stanford engineering team that won the 2005 DARPA Grand Challenge by navigating 132 desert miles.

## Safety Record & Public Scrutiny
- **Data vs. Perception:** According to an Insurance Institute for Highway Safety study across four cities, Waymo vehicles were involved in **68% fewer crashes** than human drivers and achieved a **91% lower rate** of rear-end collisions.
- **Public Hesitancy:** A **2026 Pew Research poll** revealed that **71% of adults** report feeling uncomfortable in a driverless car. Viral videos of minor operational issues—such as cars blocking traffic or honking at one another—frequently fuel public skepticism.
- **Safety Philosophy & Human Error:** Mawakana emphasizes humility regarding potential future incidents, arguing that society must weigh the imperfect status quo of human-caused traffic fatalities against autonomous safety improvements.
- **Remote Assistance Clarification:** Responding to Senate hearing disclosures, Mawakana clarified that remote operators based in locations like the Philippines provide guidance during edge cases (such as blocked emergency routes) but **do not actively drive** the vehicles remotely.

## Technology & Manufacturing
- **Vehicle Fleet & Hardware:** Waymo's current scaling relies on the electric minivan Ojai (built by Chinese automaker Zeeker and outfitted with the Waymo driver in Phoenix, Arizona) following the discontinuation of Jaguar's I-PACE model.
- **Multi-Sensor Tech Stack:** Each vehicle is equipped with:
  - **13 cameras:** Capture visual details like lane markings and traffic light colors.
  - **6 radar sensors:** Measure distance and velocity when cameras are less reliable.
  - **4 LiDAR sensors (Light Detection and Ranging):** Emit laser pulses to build a 3D picture of shapes and distances up to **three football fields away** in a 360-degree radius.
- **Manufacturing Efficiency:** Amanda Bell leads Waymo's Phoenix manufacturing site, where vehicles are fully outfitted with the sensor suite and hardware in a single work shift (one day).
- **In-House vs. Competitor Approach:** Waymo designs its entire hardware and software stack in-house, contrasting with competitors like Tesla, which relies primarily on cameras and AI trained on real-world miles while rejecting LiDAR as costly and unnecessary.

## Business Model, Competition, & Pricing
- **Trip Volume & Cost:** Waymo surpassed **500,000 trips per week** earlier this year. Rides average **$9.58 per mile**, compared to **$6.88 for Uber** and **$6.41 for Lyft**. Mawakana noted that price is not the primary immediate priority, as dynamic pricing adjusts during peak commuter times for fleet consistency.
- **Complex Partnership Dynamics:** Waymo maintains a nuanced relationship with Uber—acting as investor, rival, and partner in markets like Austin and Atlanta, even as both companies prepare to enter new markets and face labor union pushback over driver displacement.
- **Surveillance and Law Enforcement:** Waymo maintains that it does not run continuous background tape for general tracking or police monitoring; data is only shared with law enforcement under strict, down-scoped lawful processes.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Future Fleet Evolution:** Mawakana predicts that over the next 5, 10, or 20 years, a generalizable Waymo driver deployed across multiple business lines will become the standard expectation for consumers seeking safe transit from point A to point B.
- **Steering Wheel Timeline:** Mawakana claims that steering wheels will disappear "over time, absolutely," with pedals and driver seats potentially following, though Waymo has delayed this to maintain accessibility for first responders and tow truck operators.
- **Licensing Strategy:** Mawakana states that Waymo will expand beyond ride-hailing into other business lines, including licensing its autonomous technology to traditional automotive companies for retail sale.

## Notable Quotes
> "I think it's important for society to grapple with that question of how uncomfortable am I with the status quo? Is it worth it to get an improvement by embracing this new technology that isn't promising to be perfect, but at the same time, it can really improve road safety."
> — Tekedra Mawakana

> "I think that for us, our position is really we want to do strengths on strengths. We're a tech company. We have all of this incredible knowledge and know-how to be able to build an autonomous vehicle. But then on the vehicle side, there's OEMs that have been doing this for hundreds of years and they know the vehicle."
> — Tekedra Mawakana

items.title: What Happens When the AI Boom Slows Down
items.summary: Martin Casado argues that AI represents an industrial revolution rather than a software cycle, transforming engineering constraints into capital allocation problems while exposing the limitations of traditional venture mindsets.
items.content_text:
### TL;DR
Martin Casado argues that AI represents an industrial revolution rather than a software cycle, transforming engineering constraints into capital allocation problems while exposing the limitations of traditional venture mindsets.

---

## 1. Investor Mindsets & Venture Capital Realities
* **Four Investor Archetypes:** Martin Casado identifies four distinct mindsets in private markets:
  * **Traditional Finance:** Relies on SaaS metrics and market size as proxies for business health.
  * **Productive Investors:** Focuses on technical approaches, adjacent markets, technology evolution speed, and team execution.
  * **Frontier Investors:** Romanticized 1960s/70s style ("YOLO"), backing founders based purely on talent networks and visionary science fiction tropes.
  * **Speculative Investors:** Focuses exclusively on market timing rather than underlying asset growth.
* **Misapplied Financial Metrics:** Applying late-stage or traditional SaaS financial mindsets (like low gross retention or high-margin expectations) to early-stage disruptive technology is self-defeating. Disruptive technology naturally lacks established business models or immediate TAM clarity.
* **Market Efficiency:** Private markets are efficient; Casado rejects the idea of "truffle-hunting" non-consensus deals or beating the market through cleverness, viewing competitive rounds and market pricing as the norm.
* **The TAM Fallacy:** Disagrees with zero-sum views (such as those held by Sequoia's Roloff) that venture capital is overfunded; capital creates opportunities and directly expands the investable TAM.

## 2. Infrastructure Refactoring & The Agent Era
* **Infrastructure Stack Rebuild:** Infrastructure (compute, network, storage, databases, and models) is experiencing maximum disruption as it is refactored for AI and agents.
* **OLTP Databases & Networking:** 
  * Transaction databases (OLTP) are seeing net-new entrants because AI agents eliminate the need to train humans on new, non-standard database query languages.
  * High-performance GPU clusters require rigid performance constraints, driving optical networking innovations and new networking companies for the first time since Arista.
* **Software Volume Surge:** Vibe-coding and AI agents mean significantly more software is being written than ever before, which requires underlying compute, storage, and database infrastructure.

## 3. Models, Frontiers, and the Economics of Compute
* **The 3-to-6 Month Model Lifespan:** The lifespan of a frontier model is extremely short (3 to 6 months). If a frontier lab stumbles or slips by 3 months, it risks losing the entire market.
* **Competitive Equilibria in Token Usage:** Even when tasks are heavily automated, startups in competitive equilibria will always pay 10 times more for the smartest frontier model rather than a cheaper, dumber model.
* **Capital and Token Factories:** Neo-clouds function as token factories with heavy vertical integration. The real bottleneck for these providers is physical infrastructure, specifically **power supply** and **hardware chips (GPUs)**.
* **Regulatory Pressures & Space:** With over 500 proposed legislations attempting to stop data center building in the U.S. (including Texas), future compute infrastructure may increasingly move internationally or even to space.

## 4. Cybersecurity & Digital vs. Physical Scaling
* **Cybersecurity Evolution:** While AI is driving a "breach apocalypse," it mirrors the chaotic early days of the internet (such as vulnerable Windows 95 installations). The good guys will continue outspending bad guys to deliver technical security solutions, resulting in software that is ultimately much more secure.
* **Digital vs. Physical Worlds:** Digital problems can be solved by throwing capital at them via Reinforcement Learning (RL) environments. However, scaling curves and distributions for robotics, the physical universe, medicine, and science remain unpredictable and unproven.

## 5. Strategic M&A and Deal Dynamics
* **Strategic Exits:** Casado has participated in massive strategic M&A deals (including VMware, Tabular, Cursor, and World Labs). Key drivers include deep personal alignment between buyers and founders, and presenting a clear base case plus an inductive step (buying an option on a massive market).
* **Deal Killers:** Leaking deals to the press and treating strategic M&A like a poker game or a competitive auction destabilizes transactions. Buyers like Mark Zuckerberg or Lisa Su are deeply sophisticated and require trust, good faith, and professional alignment.

---

## Notable Quotes

items.title: Why Datasite Stopped Building Its Own Parsing - Adit Abraham, Reducto & Raj Bakhru, Datasite
items.summary: Datasite global CTO Raj Bakhru and Reducto CEO Adit Abraham discuss scaling AI across virtual data rooms handling 60% of $100M+ deals, explaining why outsourcing document parsing to Reducto allowed Datasite's 250 engineers to focus on high-value GraphRAG and agentic products.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Datasite global CTO Raj Bakhru and Reducto CEO Adit Abraham discuss scaling AI across virtual data rooms handling 60% of $100M+ deals, explaining why outsourcing document parsing to Reducto allowed Datasite's 250 engineers to focus on high-value GraphRAG and agentic products.

## Background & Scale of Datasite
- **Company Leadership:** Raj Bakhru serves as Global CTO at Datasite; Adit Abraham is Co-founder and CEO at Reducto.
- **Transaction Volume:** Datasite handles approximately 60% of all global corporate transactions over $100 million.
- **Platform Scale:** 
  - Over 500,000 monthly active users accessing content.
  - Generates a trillion-plus tokens per year.
  - Processes 55,000 virtual data rooms (VDRs) a year.
  - Experienced 40% top-line growth over the 18 months following the BlueFlame acquisition.

## The BlueFlame Acquisition Journey
- **Founding & Bootstrap:** Raj Bakhru co-founded the vertical AI M&A startup BlueFlame after running M&A/strategy for a security firm he previously sold. BlueFlame bootstrapped initially to save costs.
- **The Acquisition:** Approached Datasite for a $5 million investment round during VC fundraising, which resulted in Datasite acquiring the 50-person company instead over a dinner meeting.
- **Competitive Pressure:** BlueFlame realized that competing against venture-backed vertical AI rivals (who raised hundreds of millions) and well-funded frontier model labs would require massive dilution, prompting the acquisition.
- **Proprietary Data Advantage:** The acquisition combined BlueFlame with Datasite's VDR ecosystem and Grata (a private company database with 20 million companies), creating an isolated, highly differentiated proprietary data moat.

## Parsing Challenges & The Build vs. Buy Strategy
- **The Endless Edge Cases:** Scrapily built ingestion pipelines failed on complex financial documents. Edge cases included:
  - Pie charts failing because a legend's shade of blue didn't correlate perfectly with the LLM's interpretation.
  - Complex Excel spreadsheets featuring merged cells, XLSB macro-enabled files, and templates.
- **Engineering Allocation:** Datasite employs 250 engineers divided across 5 major revenue-generating initiatives. 
- **Outsourcing Logic:** Bakhru determined that supporting document extraction mechanics was a solved problem not worth consuming valuable engineering bandwidth, leading Datasite to partner with Reducto.

## Architecture & Evaluation (VDR Bench)
- **Data Ingestion Pipeline:** Large bursts of transaction data (up to a terabyte dropped instantly by bankers) pass through Reducto within Datasite's secure environment.
- **Vector Storage & GraphRAG:** Processed data feeds into Turbo Buffer as the vector database, powering GraphRAG queries executed via Python code.
- **VDR Bench:** Datasite's internal evaluation benchmark consisting of hundreds of documents and hundreds of questions with known answers.
- **Evaluation Results:** Upgrading parsing with Reducto improved VDR Bench recall by **22%**, outperforming direct off-the-shelf frontier lab tools (such as Claude Projects or OpenAI Projects).

## Notable Quotes
> *"It's all edge cases. Like literally everything is an edge case... the devil's in the details on all of this stuff."*
> — Raj Bakhru

> *"If I can outsource everything on the layers underneath that [core business logic], that's an ideal split of time for my team."*
> — Raj Bakhru

> *"A lot of people think that sort of all the work needs to be done on the other side, the answering side, and most of the work actually is on the extraction side. You get that right, and everything else can follow."*
> — Raj Bakhru

items.summary: Morgan Stanley CEO Ted Pick projects cumulative AI infrastructure spending will reach $10–$15 trillion over the next decade, while PIMCO CEO Manny Roman asserts that global sovereign debt markets remain "well anchored" and that high interest rates are driven primarily by Middle East developments and the energy complex rather than AI financing.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Morgan Stanley CEO Ted Pick projects cumulative AI infrastructure spending will reach $10–$15 trillion over the next decade, while PIMCO CEO Manny Roman asserts that global sovereign debt markets remain "well anchored" and that high interest rates are driven primarily by Middle East developments and the energy complex rather than AI financing.

## AI Infrastructure Boom & Capital Expenditure (Ted Pick)
* **Scale of Investment:** 
  * Cumulative AI CapEx is projected to reach **$10–$15 trillion** over the next 7 to 12 years.
  * Current AI spending is in the **"second or third inning,"** running at roughly **$1 trillion a year** for the next several years.
  * By comparison, total Asian CapEx is **$11 trillion** currently and is projected to reach **$16 trillion** by **2030**.
* **ROI & Urgency:** 
  * Enterprise demand currently outstrips supply, forcing companies to pay up to secure compute power rather than fall behind competitors.
  * While not every project will succeed, efficiency and effectiveness gains are expected to bring **50 to 70 basis points of real GDP growth** to the global economy.
* **Financing & Execution Risk:** 
  * Local-level resistance (NIMBYism) creates localized completion and location risks that will command risk premiums in capital structures.
  * Morgan Stanley acts as a trusted advisor to help structure deals, determining the appropriate mix of debt, equity, and private securities (such as through their recent acquisition of **Equity Zen**).

## Sovereign Debt, Central Banks, & Macro Economics (Manny Roman)
* **Sovereign Markets & Interest Rates:** 
  * Sovereign debt markets are **"well anchored,"** evidenced by stable swap spreads and TIPS.
  * High interest rates are driven by the Middle East and the energy complex, not the **$500 billion** of AI financing to date.
* **Central Bank Trajectory:** 
  * In the US, the Federal Reserve is expected to raise rates by **a quarter point** at the end of the year and then pause.
  * In Europe, central banks likely need to raise rates **twice** due to worse macroeconomic conditions, characterized by low growth, high debt-to-GDP, and heavy taxation.
* **Currency & Global Reserves:** 
  * The US dollar remains the primary reserve currency due to a lack of attractive currency diversification alternatives, ensuring the strength of the dollar is likely to persist.
  * For China, the single most important macro decision over the next 20 years will be whether to let the yuan float.

## Fixed Income & Investment Strategy (Manny Roman)
* **Yield Attractiveness:** 
  * Fixed income offers a blended return of **7% to 8%**, which looks highly attractive on a risk-adjusted basis compared to expensive S&P 500 equity valuations.
  * PIMCO is seeing strong rebalancing trends toward fixed income across the US, Europe, and Asia.
* **Specific Opportunities:** 
  * **US and Global Markets:** US sovereign debt and mortgages look very attractive.
  * **Emerging Markets & Alternatives:** Emerging markets offer numerous opportunities, and private structured finance/asset-backed assets are generating **12% to 15%** returns (including building data centers in Europe).
* **Inflation & Long-Term Drivers:** 
  * AI is CapEx-intensive upfront from strong hands, but **long-term deflationary**, aided by future labor market shifts driven by robotics.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* Cumulative AI infrastructure spending will reach **$10–$15 trillion** over the next decade (Ted Pick).
* The AI investment timeline will span **7 to 12 years** (Ted Pick).
* AI higher intelligence and productivity will add **50 to 70 basis points** of real GDP growth to the global economy (Ted Pick).
* The Federal Reserve will raise rates by **a quarter point** at the end of the year and stop (Manny Roman).

## Notable Quotes
> "We're somewhere in the second or third inning... we're going to have to see. But I think the kind of ranges we're seeing right now are about a trillion a year for the next several years."
> — Ted Pick

> "Our view is that if you look at the swap spread or if you look at TIPS, the market is very well anchored. And that's the reason why rates are high is because of what's happening in the Middle East and what's happening in the energy complex."
> — Manny Roman

items.title: A quiet investor’s $10 billion bet on AI, chips, and defense
items.summary: Alex Davis, founder of Dallas-based Disruptive, has launched a new $10 billion fund to concentrate massive growth-stage capital on roughly 10 elite "N of one" companies—such as Palantir, Groq, Databricks, and Shield AI—leveraging an active, relationship-heavy approach that includes executive-level storytelling, global business development, and hands-on operational leadership.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Alex Davis, founder of Dallas-based Disruptive, has launched a new $10 billion fund to concentrate massive growth-stage capital on roughly 10 elite "N of one" companies—such as Palantir, Groq, Databricks, and Shield AI—leveraging an active, relationship-heavy approach that includes executive-level storytelling, global business development, and hands-on operational leadership.

## Investment Strategy & the Macro Environment
* **The "Haves and Have-Nots" Reality:** 
  * **Parabolic Unicorn Growth:** The market has expanded from roughly 10 venture-backed unicorns in 2011 to 5,000–6,000 today.
  * **The End of Garage Computing:** Modern frontier AI models cannot be built on a family budget or bootstrapping savings; compute realities separate the dominant players from companies that will struggle or get acquired.
* **Concentrated Offense Over Spray-and-Pray:** 
  * **The 10-Company Thesis:** Disruptive targets a hyper-focused list of the top 15-20 companies globally, deploying capital into roughly 10 distinct entities via large, concentrated checks.
  * **Proprietary Sourcing:** The firm actively identifies and pursues target companies rather than relying on inbound pitch decks, viewing inbound deal flow as adverse selection.
* **Value Investing is Dead:** 
  * **Exponential Outcomes:** Davis argues that obsessing over a 5% to 15% valuation discount is a mistake; generational returns are driven entirely by backing great, exponential companies regardless of premium pricing.

## Compute, Neoclouds, & AI Infrastructure
* **The Compute Shortage & Neoclouds:** 
  * **Infrastructure Necessity:** A massive, prevalent compute shortage requires neoclouds and sophisticated financing to stand up and operate infrastructure.
  * **Speculative Landlords Warned:** Davis cautioned against speculative landlords without proper funding, experience, or chip access—predicting failure for players sitting on raw land in Texas relying on debt without deep infrastructure expertise.
* **Compute Efficiency & Frontier Costs:** 
  * **No Shortcuts to Frontier Quality:** Despite social media claims of models achieving frontier performance for $10,000 in compute via distillation, Davis asserts these do not meet the rigorous demands of sovereign customers or major financial institutions.

## Palantir & Groq Case Studies
* **Palantir (Pre-IPO Conviction):** 
  * **Decade-Long Backing:** Disruptive invested consistently in Palantir for roughly 10 years, recognizing their out-competition for engineering talent and ability to create entirely new enterprise budgets.
  * **Doubling Down Pre-IPO:** Right before Palantir's direct listing during COVID, Disruptive doubled down with a large insurance partner, betting heavily on Alex Karp's unique leadership and ability to win over public markets.
* **Groq (Inference & Operational Takeover):** 
  * **The Nvidia Licensing Deal:** Following Nvidia's non-exclusive $20 billion licensing deal for Groq (which saw Jonathan and core team members move to Nvidia), Disruptive stepped in to ensure tax-efficient shareholder distributions.
  * **Running the Company:** Alex Davis took over the board chair and operational reins of Groq's remaining assets, upgrading 53 existing megawatts of compute, shifting into liquid-cooled sites, and positioning the infrastructure as an inference neocloud to serve portfolio companies and hyperscalers.

## Fund Structure & Private Market Risks
* **Shift to Discretionary Capital:** 
  * **SPV Vulnerabilities:** While Disruptive historically relied on large SPVs, changing market dynamics and a proliferation of grey-market brokers/SPVs with unverified capital calls have created regulatory risks and potential "black eyes" for premier private companies (e.g., Anthropic, Databricks, SpaceX).
  * **Committed Institutional Fund:** The new $10 billion fund provides secure, transparent, and committed capital directly matching what top-tier private companies demand.
* **Disruptive Firm Architecture:** 
  * **Lean and Aligned:** Operating with a team of roughly 30 employees, Disruptive rejects traditional AUM-chasing management fee bloat, earning its returns strictly through performance carry.

## Defense Tech & Sovereign AI Opportunities
* **New Prime Contractors:** 
  * **Breaking the Century-Old Mold:** Private companies like Shield AI (which recently signed massive contracts with the Navy) are successfully building relationships with the US and foreign governments, paving the way for the first new defense prime contractors in 100 years.
  * **AI and the Pentagon:** Because frontier models require heavy regulatory navigation, safety frameworks, and national security integrations, AI companies are effectively evolving into defense companies.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* "Open source will dominate AI inferencing within 2 years" — *Wait, check transcript:* The transcript notes Alex Davis stating open weights/US open weights represent a massive opportunity because Western companies want to own their own stack and see competition to closed models, but **no strict 2-year timeline was stated**. (Omit or reframe strictly to stated claims).
* *Correction:* Per instructions, only include predictions with exact timeframes/numbers/conditions stated by speakers.
* **Alex Davis:** Predicts a massive, multi-billion-dollar market opportunity in safety and corporate data protection against the growth and populism of AI.
* **Alex Davis:** Predicts the emergence of new defense prime contractors outside of the hundred-year-old incumbents, driven by innovators scaling independent tech stacks for the US government.
* **Alex Davis:** Predicts that speculative neocloud landlords lacking proper funding, offtakers, or chip access will fail under the weight of rising memory costs (5x over two years) and rapid chip iteration cycles.

## Notable Quotes
> "If you really dumb it down... to the top half a dozen 20 companies or so, I think those opportunities exist. And what's happening with those is they've gotten so big and they've stayed private longer... the need for capital for the very best companies in the world as they stay private is abundant and I think they deserve the capital and so therefore people like us should be writing larger concentrated checks."
> — Alex Davis

> "The idea of my node is like let me go get that at a 6% discount... Enthropic is good if I can get it at a 6% discount or I'm not doing it. Like that was the value investing mentality... and my argument is like buy a great company period... the great outcomes were exponential outcomes."
> — Alex Davis

> "If you're a visitor to the space, I think that... I could see a lot of people getting hurt, putting a lot of debt on these projects and finding out that, forget about offtakers, they never end up with chips."
> — Alex Davis

items.title: Andrew Huberman on Focus, Energy, and Performing at Your Best
items.summary: Andrew Huberman and Daisy Wolf discuss evidence-based health and cognitive protocols—ranging from morning sunlight and high-efficiency resistance training to targeted supplementation and sleep optimization—while emphasizing that protocols must serve life rather than constrain it.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Andrew Huberman and Daisy Wolf discuss evidence-based health and cognitive protocols—ranging from morning sunlight and high-efficiency resistance training to targeted supplementation and sleep optimization—while emphasizing that protocols must serve life rather than constrain it.

## Daily Health Protocols & Movement
- **Morning Routine:** 
  - **Sunlight Exposure:** Andrew Huberman gets bright light (ideally sunlight, or a 10,000-lux artificial light if dark) in his eyes within the first 30–60 minutes of waking.
  - **Meditation & Caffeine:** Huberman does a 5-minute breathing meditation to observe mental chaos, then drinks yerba mate immediately if exercising, or delays if not.
- **Resistance Training (35-Year Protocol):**
  - **Structure:** 3 days per week lifting weights; 2–3 days of cardio (e.g., 1-minute warm-up, followed by 8 rounds of 20 seconds all-out effort and 10 seconds rest).
  - **Lifting Execution:** Uses a light warm-up set (10–12 reps), a moderate preparation set (doing only 3 out of 10 possible reps), and exactly 2 all-out work sets taken to momentary muscular failure with 3–4 minutes of rest.
  - **Progression:** Increase weight or reps every single workout.
- **Nutrition & Diet:**
  - **Post-Workout & Meals:** Huberman eats starches/fruit (banana, blueberry, whey, oatmeal, sourdough with butter and salt) after heavy training to replenish glycogen. Lunch typically consists of grilled steak, sliced cucumbers, tomatoes, and rice with olive oil.
  - **Dietary Experiments:** Avoids fibrous foods like broccoli and high-histamine foods like onions that cause gastric distress or post-meal sleepiness. Uses digestive enzymes and histamine-blocking enzymes to expand dietary flexibility.
- **Evening Wind-Down:**
  - **Non-Sleep Deep Rest (NSDR):** Utilizes 10–30 minutes of yoga nidra in the afternoon to restore vigor without sleep inertia.
  - **Evening Light & Sleep:** Stops caffeine by 2:00 PM, dims lights, wears red-lens blue-light blocking glasses (Roka), and avoids screens before sleeping around 11:00 PM.

## Supplementation Stack
- **Foundational Supplements:**
  - **AG1:** Taken twice daily (morning and evening) to cover nutritional gaps.
  - **Omega-3s:** Takes **Lovaza** (prescription omega-3, >1 gram of EPA per day) for heavy-metal-free cardiovascular and anti-inflammatory support.
  - **Vitamin D3:** Takes **3,000 to 5,000 units** daily.
- **Targeted & Performance Supplements:**
  - **Tongkat Ali:** Takes **400 milligrams** (Solaray version) daily to unbind sex hormone binding globulin from testosterone.
  - **P5P (Vitamin B6 derivative):** Takes **50 milligrams** in the morning to slightly reduce prolactin and amplify catecholamines.
  - **N-Acetylcysteine (NAC):** Takes **600 milligrams** daily (up to 3 times daily when traveling or feeling run down) as a glutathione precursor and flu/cold preventative.
  - **Digestive Support:** Uses a multivitamin, digestive enzymes, and histamine-blocking enzymes with lunch.
  - **Sleep Support:** Takes **AGZ** (magnesium threonate, tart cherry extract cocktail) in the evening to promote deep sleep.

## Cognitive Performance & Founder Strategies
- **Protecting Peak Focus Windows:** 
  - **Huberman’s Windows:** Peak cognitive capacity occurs from **9:30 AM to 12:30 PM** and **4:30 PM to 7:00 PM**.
  - **Execution:** Founders must identify and fiercely protect their personal high-focus windows like a physical fight, avoiding distractions to maximize exponential productivity.
- **Phone & Social Media Management:** 
  - Huberman keeps X and Instagram on a separate phone locked inside a supermax prison lock box to eliminate unconscious time-sucks and preserve cognitive resources.
- **Sustainable Workloads:** 
  - Avoid chronic stimulant-driven burnout; treat career longevity like an endurance event by establishing a sustainable maximum of real work paired with weekly disengagement (e.g., hiking in nature).

## Notable Quotes
> "The best way I can describe this practice in terms of its utility is just as with exercise if you get a burn in your legs or the final repetitions of lifting weights, that's what triggers the adaptation with meditation in terms of consciousness and and focus and awareness. I think the lactate of the mind... is to be able to experience that chaos, observe it and not do anything with it."
> — **Andrew Huberman**

> "If you're going to do things for your health, they have to support the other areas of your life in a way that feed back onto something where your company succeeds and then you actually have the resources to maybe change your schedule someday. But otherwise, if people are trying to just pack all these protocols in, they're just going to deplete themselves."
> — **Andrew Huberman**

> "Figure out the maximum amount of real work that you can do every day consistently, and then figure out some non-destructive way to reset yourself every single week."
> — **Bob Knight** (cited by Andrew Huberman)

items.title: Earnings Special: Apple's Forecast Disappoints, Despite Topping Estimates | Bloomberg Tech
items.summary: Apple reported a Q4 earnings beat with $114.48 billion in revenue and $2.10 EPS, driven by strong iPhone sales (particularly the iPhone 18 Pro), though Greater China revenue missed expectations at $17.54 billion.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Apple reported a Q4 earnings beat with $114.48 billion in revenue and $2.10 EPS, driven by strong iPhone sales (particularly the iPhone 18 Pro), though Greater China revenue missed expectations at $17.54 billion.

## Q4 Financial Performance & Metrics
- **Top-Line Beat:** Fourth-quarter revenue reached $114.48 billion, topping the Street estimate of $113.47 billion (and noted elsewhere as $114.5 billion).
- **Bottom-Line Beat:** Fourth-quarter earnings per share (EPS) came in at $2.10, beating expectations by $0.10.
- **Segment Breakdown:**
  - **iPhone Revenue:** Beat estimates at $57.58 billion (compared to the $56.49 billion estimate).
  - **Services Revenue:** Met expectations nearly exactly at $31.57 billion (estimate was $31.58 billion).
  - **Products Revenue:** Came in above estimates at $82.9 billion.
  - **Other Segments:** Wearables and iPad revenue both missed expectations; Mac revenue and Americas revenue came in just above estimates.
  - **Operating Expenses:** Total operating expenses landed in line with estimates at $19.19 billion.
- **Greater China Struggles:** Greater China revenue missed estimates again, coming in at $17.54 billion versus the expected $18.75 billion.

## iPhone & Hardware Product Dynamics
- **Driver of the Beat:** The earnings beat was led by sales of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, alongside continued demand for the iPhone 17 Pro/Pro Max and early-quarter carrier deals.
- **Product Pipeline Context:** 
  - The report arrived despite a minor year-over-year upgrade cycle for the iPhone 18 Pro, the absence of a regular iPhone 18 or iPhone Air 2 at launch, and major fall products (Touch MacBook Pro, Home View, HomePod Mini, Apple TV, OLED iPad) delayed until the holiday quarter.
- **iPhone Duo Supply & Demand:** 
  - Early reception and demand for the iPhone Duo have been exceptionally strong, bolstered by Apple's lease plan.
  - Unit projections for the year sit at approximately 15 million units.
  - Supply shortages are severe; pre-orders for many buyers do not launch until late January, and physical retail units are nearly impossible for human consumers to acquire due to AI bot buying.
  - Hardware defects: Early-batch screen cracking issues on the iPhone Duo have seen a dramatic slowdown, indicating an isolated early manufacturing defect rather than a systemic color or regional flaw.

## Strategic Growth Drivers & Geographic Markets
- **China vs. India:** 
  - China remains Apple's most important near-term unit growth driver over the next 3 years, despite recent tough comparisons following previous 22%–28% growth quarters.
  - India is an increasingly important aspirational market with expanding middle-class affluence and newly opened retail stores, though its overall revenue contribution remains small and per capita income lags behind China.
- **Services & AI Search Headwinds:** 
  - Services revenue growth has decelerated to around the 10% mark over the past two quarters.
  - A significant portion of services revenue relies on Google search revenue-sharing within Safari; as users migrate toward AI chat apps (ChatGPT, Claude, Muse, Gemini), Google search volume—and subsequently Apple's revenue share—faces downward pressure.

## Leadership & Corporate Strategy Under John Turnus
- **Continuity Over Overhaul:** Under new CEO John Turnus (a product executive), Apple's core strategy remains steady as current initiatives were multi-year developments under Tim Cook.
- **Cost Discipline:** Turnus is pushing the company to run faster and leaner, marked by both under-the-radar and visible layoffs alongside broader cost-cutting measures.
- **Revenue Smoothing:** The launch timing of devices like the iPhone Duo aligns with a broader goal under Turnus to create more consistent revenue distribution across the entire year rather than overloading the back-end holiday quarter.

## AI Strategy & Competitive Position
- **Market Valuation:** Apple entered the earnings print as the best-performing "Magnificent Seven" stock, up roughly 25% year-to-date and holding an enviable free cash flow position compared to heavy-spending AI hyperscalers.
- **The AI Assistant Gap:** Despite solid financial performance, critics point out a lack of evidence that Apple has built a native, competitive conversational AI agent on par with standalone consumer tools like ChatGPT, Claude, or Muse.
- **Siri AI Evaluation:** Siri AI functions effectively as an execution layer for routine phone tasks (utilizing the Gemini model for 90% of basic use cases), fulfilling the original 15-year-old vision of Siri, but it falls short of acting as a true, human-like general-purpose real-world digital assistant.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **China Growth:** China will remain Apple's most important near-term growth driver over the next 3 years — Anurag Rana.
- **iPhone Duo Unit Sales:** Apple will sell about 15 million units of the iPhone Duo this year — Anurag Rana.
- **Availability Timeline:** Consumers will be able to easily walk into a store and buy an iPhone Duo without severe inventory constraints by February or March — Mark Gurman.
- **Political Impact:** The midterm election outcome will have zero impact on Apple's business operations or political navigation — Mark Gurman.

## Notable Quotes
> *"Gross margins, you know, tell me how you're going to maintain gross margins over the next I would say three to four quarters with memory prices up costs going so high. And then what are you doing with your supply chain to ensure that people have and get the phones that they need uh in you know, in the right amount of time."* — **Anurag Rana**

> *"We've seen zero evidence from Apple that they're successful—that they're going to be able to successfully take advantage of that cash holding and trade that in for a strong AI strategy."* — **Mark Gurman**

> *"The iPhone duo is a game-changing experience. And I think if you really should give it a shot. I mean, I've seen some people buy it and return it, but give it the 2 weeks and I think you'll get used to it. The inner screen is simply incredible. It's changed my workflow completely."* — **Mark Gurman**

items.title: End of the Internet | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
items.summary: The open public internet as a global platform is dying due to AI-driven security vulnerabilities, bot-filled content slop, and hyper-competition, forcing a return to smaller, private, and trusted spaces like group chats and niche subscription models.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
The open public internet as a global platform is dying due to AI-driven security vulnerabilities, bot-filled content slop, and hyper-competition, forcing a return to smaller, private, and trusted spaces like group chats and niche subscription models.

## The End of Blogging and the Rise of Subscriptions
* **Early Blogosphere Origins:** Early blogging waves in the early 2000s were dominated by political and niche content creators (e.g., Talking Points Memo, Andrew Sullivan, Boing Boing, Instapundit, Matt Yglesias, Daily Kos, Daring Fireball, AVC).
* **The Google Aggregation Trap:** While distribution was free, Google captured discovery and most ad revenue through AdSense, eventually leading to intrusive ads and shrinking payouts as content supply became limitless.
* **The Subscription Pivot:** 
  * Andrew Sullivan proved the viability of reader-supported models, earning nearly $1 million a year over his final two years through loyal readers.
  * Ben Thompson noted that going small and niche—limiting audience size to serve customers who truly care—is a more sustainable business model than milking ad pennies from everyone.

## The Evolution of Social Media into Group Chats
* **The Decay of Public Platforms:** Social media followed the 99-1 rule (1% speak, 9% comment, 90% lurk), eventually prioritizing engagement metrics and transforming public networks into personal entertainment sites like TikTok with zero social component.
* **The Group Chat Renaissance:** 
  * Public social media has hollowed out, but social networking itself is stronger than ever inside private, high-trust group chats.
  * The modern winning scale is not an ever-larger audience, but the proliferation of infinite finite groups where users feel safe to communicate.

## The Collapse of the Public Internet and Software Security
* **Current Security Vulnerabilities:** Recent security failures include critical PHP remote code execution bugs (patched automatically on Shurtugal via Pressable), compromised intermediate CA private keys, and major vulnerabilities in node.js, GitLab, Java, Cisco products, and LLM supply chains.
* **The AI Threat Multiplier:** 
  * Software has historically been built on creaky, human-authored foundations where the primary gate was functionality rather than security.
  * AI possesses limitless time and the ability to substitute iteration for cleverness, exposing vulnerabilities faster than human defenders can patch them.
* **The Death of DIY Hosting:** Setting up your own public website, server, or app from scratch has become a dangerous proposition in the age of AI, turning the public internet into a battle zone and wasteland.

## The Shift to No-Code and Bespoke Software
* **Private and Internal Apps:** Instead of building public apps for the App Store (which will be flooded with AI slop), creators are building internal software for themselves and small, trusted teams (e.g., Ben Thompson's Shady Acres apps for podcast production, task tracking, and calendar management).
* **Democratized Creation:** AI eliminates the high upfront costs traditionally required to justify large audiences, making it possible to build customized software for a single person or team.

## Cognitive Capitalism and Economic Transformation
* **Venkatesh Rao’s "Cognitive Mercantilism":** Draws a parallel between the agricultural revolution—which liberated humans from subsistence farming to create industrial markets—and the AI revolution, which frees human minds from "subsistence cognition."
* **Competing Views on AI Intelligence:**
  * *AI Malthusian:* Sees an oversupply of intelligence that outruns humanity, creating economically redundant minds.
  * *Cognitive Capitalist:* Sees an expansion of demand from minds liberated to pursue previously unfulfillable cognitive desires.
* **The Power of Association:** Citing Alexis de Tocqueville’s *Democracy in America*, the future points toward infinite local markets and voluntary associations rather than monolithic global platforms, creating diverse opportunities to meet new human needs.

## Infrastructure and Ecosystem Support (Stripe Partnership)
* **Foundation for Internet-Native Companies:** Stripe provides the underlying infrastructure for modern internet businesses, including Substack (where every creator is a Stripe customer), fintech card programs, multi-participant marketplaces, and usage-based AI companies.
* **Enabling Experimentation:** While Stripe does not answer foundational business questions about product-market fit, it removes the heavy lifting of onboarding, payouts, and billing, making it practical to try new business models.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* Ben Thompson expects software security vulnerabilities to get worse before they get better, driven by AI-accelerated attacks (*"I expect things to only get worse... it's going to get worse before it gets better, which I do, for the record, expect to happen"*).
* Ben Thompson predicts that in the long run, software will improve because it will be rewritten by AI and defended continuously by agents (*"After all, the good guys have AI as well, and in the long run software will be better when it is rewritten by AI and defended by agents continuously"*).

## Notable Quotes
> "In short, the answer to drowning in abundance is to purposely limit your audience, to go small. That is an economic model that works..."
> — Ben Thompson

> "The most important consequence of the agricultural revolution was not that farming became more efficient. It was that most people were liberated from the necessity of farming, allowing entirely new kinds of economic and cultural life to emerge."
> — Venkatesh Rao (cited by Ben Thompson)
